about.text: The Armenian name (չորթան) for dried tan, the buttermilk left after butter is churned from matsun; dried into a hard, keeping food like the qurut of Central Asia.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.label: heat, dry
how.text: Chortan ('dry tan') is the Armenian dried product made by heating and straining diluted yoghurt and drying the curd, the Armenian counterpart of kashk and qurut.
